what: The Claude Code device — CC's presence in the Cairn rack. Its shim receives bus messages and pokes CC of them; its probes let the ground loop fire health checks each beat. Without this device the cocoon strategy has no address to deliver work to, and a second Cairn instance cannot spin up its own CC.
why: CC is the primary resolver in the system, but it had no address in the rack — no charter, no shim, no probes. Two filed tickets (superclaude-tmux-mode, cc-chat-pane-via-hook-append) are pieces that belong to a device that did not exist. The cocoon wraps CC (memory cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc), but the thing being wrapped needs a rack address for the wrapper to find.
how: A device class at cairn/devices/cc/ following the established pattern: (1) this charter defining CC's role, ownership, and learning; (2) a shim inheriting BaseShim — device_id 'cc', probes loaded by discover(), messages received via deliver(); (3) probes the ground loop fires each beat; (4) instance 0 at ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/. The device composes BaseShim (lifecycle, message routing) and the Probe pattern (heartbeat-driven monitoring). CC's process is NOT started by this device — CC starts itself; the shim only gives it a rack address.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) cairn/devices/cc/ does not exist with an intention+why.json charter, a shim inheriting BaseShim, and at least one probe; (2) the ground loop's discover() does not find the device and load its probes with zero failures; (3) a message sent through the bus to device_id 'cc' does not reach the shim's deliver() — verified by sending a test message and observing it arrive in the shim's diagnostic mailbox.

gates.proof_gate: tester runs probes via discover() — the device's probe folder loads with zero failures, the shim inherits BaseShim and arms on instantiation, and a message round-trips through deliver()
gates.durability_gate: git commit — cairn/devices/cc/ and its contents are committed and pushed

owner: CC gates writes to its own device class; Akien gates the design.
how_it_learns: The shim's probes monitor CC's operational state — session liveness, message delivery reach. Probe findings travel the bus to the harbor master. The device does not learn autonomously; it is the subject of other devices' learning (the cocoon's cheaper stages learn about CC's patterns).
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: the shim driving CC on idle is the system doing its own work.
Design: cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc — cheaper stages pre-process around CC.
Design: implementation-order-claude-first — CC is the first consumer of its own automation.
The ruled ladder: ground loop → rack → CC's shim → Akien's shim → web server → librarian.
learns: It does not learn itself; CC's learning is via the trees and learning blocks, not this device's own machinery.
